messages:
khaled (EngPlat): Heads-up — we need a short design decision on allowing per-API-key overrides for internal services/partners. current problem: partner integrations occasionally need higher burst for onboarding jobs, but org-level quotas block them and support has to escalate.

maria (EngPlat): +1. We get a ticket every week. Question: should overrides be dynamic (TTL) or permanent? also who can create them? :thinking:

sam (Infra): Prefer TTL-based. Permanent overrides are hard to audit and bite later. Suggest default TTL 7d with option for 30/90d on approval.

jin (Product): From product POV: we need a console UX for audit + a simple flag in API keys to show override status. Also surface current effective qps/burst in the key details page.

liam (Security): We need RBAC around who can request/approve overrides, and every override must be logged with justification. No silent overrides by SRE on prod without ticket.

anya (Partner Success): For partners, we sometimes need temporary 10x burst for data migrations. If we can make the request flow self-service (request -> auto-approve if within safe bounds) that'd reduce ops burden.

khaled (EngPlat): Proposed enforcement model:

1) default check order on each request: per-key override -> per-org quota -> per-product quota -> global rate limiter
2) overrides are stored as scoped rules with fields: key_pattern, qps, burst, ttl, created_by, reason
3) overrides cannot exceed a safe ceiling (e.g., 10k qps or admin-configured) — safety cap enforced in code

Example override record (pseudo YAML):
```
key_overrides:
  - key_pattern: "internal-ps-*"
    qps: 50
    burst: 400
    ttl: 7d
    created_by: "anya"
    reason: "onboarding migration for partner X"
```

sam (Infra): Implementation notes:
- enforcement point lives in front of the router so we can short-circuit before routing decisions
- store overrides in Dynamo (low-latency read) with local memcache replication for hot keys
- changes should propagate via pub/sub to all serving nodes, with a 5s staleness SL

maria (EngPlat): UX story: "Request override" button in console that requires: target key, requested qps/burst, ttl, justification, linked ticket. If qps <= auto-approve-threshold (say 200 qps) then auto-approve; otherwise route to EngPlat on-call queue.

liam (Security): Also require an attest checkbox for sensitive partners. And ensure KMS audit backed logging for who approved.

jin (Product): Metrics we need on dashboard: count of active overrides, avg TTL, approvals by approver, and number of requests auto-approved vs manual. Also expose per-key effective limit in the key detail page.

anya (Partner Success): Can we also provide a "test override" mode for partners to validate migrations without changing production limits? maybe a blue-green: route 5% of partner traffic through modified limits.

khaled (EngPlat): 5% traffic routing increases complexity. alternative: sandbox keys in staging with identical infra. But we can include a 1% canary flag for specially-instrumented partners.

sam (Infra): Will need telemetry hooks: emit events for override_apply, override_revoke, override_expire, and per-request metadata which override id applied. ratebot can surface counts.

ratebot: override_apply: id=ovr-2026-03-18-001, key_pattern=internal-ps-*, qps=50, burst=400, ttl=7d

maria (EngPlat): Nice. Rollout plan: feature-flag the check order behind ff: key-override-enforcement. Phase 1: read-only enforcement (log-only) for 48h. Phase 2: gated rollout to internal orgs. Phase 3: full rollout.

jin (Product): Timeline: 2 weeks to implement basic store + enforcement, 1 week for console UX + auto-approve flow, 1 week for telemetry and dashboards.

liam (Security): Approvals: any override > 500 qps or > 24h TTL needs two-person approval and security review.

anya (Partner Success): Operational runbook: when a partner reports rate-limited errors, PS should open ticket -> request override -> monitor metrics for 24h -> revoke if not needed.

khaled (EngPlat): Implementation checklist:
- [ ] schema for overrides
- [ ] enforcement in router
- [ ] pub/sub propagation
- [ ] memcache fallback
- [ ] console button + request flow
- [ ] metrics/events
- [ ] RBAC + audit
- [ ] safety caps

sam (Infra): I'll spin up a spike branch for the enforcement hook. tagging @maria for API shape.

maria (EngPlat): I'll draft console mocks and a simple API endpoint: POST /internal/keys/overrides

jin (Product): Should the API be internal-only? we probably want console + internal API; external partners shouldn't call it directly.

liam (Security): Keep it internal-only. Any external self-service must go through Partner Success with explicit guardrails.

anya (Partner Success): Sounds good. I'll start compiling common migration request templates.

khaled (EngPlat): Ok — next steps: sam + khaled build spike, maria produce mock, jin coordinate timeline. If no objections I'll open a RFC doc later today and link it.

anya (Partner Success): one more ask: can we add a "reason" taxonomy so we can aggregate why overrides were requested (onboarding, migration, batch,test,other)?

maria (EngPlat): Yes, add reason_category: [onboarding,migration,batch,test,other]

ratebot: reminder: override_expire: id=ovr-2026-03-11-004 expired for key_pattern=internal-alpha-*

khaled (EngPlat): good catch. expiry automation must send an email + slack alert to the owner and revoke automatically. we'll include that in runbook.

sam (Infra): I'll follow up with PR for the enforcement spike in ~48h.

maria (EngPlat): Thanks everyone. I'll start the RFC and attach the console mocks. :thumbsup:
